claim: The CMP 170HX ships with two independent PCIe restrictions: a Gen1 2.5 GT/s speed cap enforced by OTP fuses plus a signed DevInit table, and an x4 width cap caused by 12 of 16 lanes shipping with their AC-coupling capacitors physically depopulated; defeating either does nothing for the other.
stance_target: The repo's hardware-table claim that the box's fabric is PCIe Gen2 x4, and its pre-flight requirement to check negotiated width and speed separately
scope_conditions: Stock CMP 170HX board; speed cap lives in silicon and SPI flash, width cap on the PCB
quoted_support: A stock CMP 170HX trains at PCIe Gen1 (2.5 GT/s) by x4. Those are two entirely separate restrictions that happen to coexist on the same board, and defeating either one does nothing whatsoever for the other.

claim: Width beyond x4 requires the AC-coupling capacitor mod: 12 of 16 lanes have their capacitors omitted, two per differential pair, so 24 x 0402 parts must be hand-soldered; lanes 0-3 are populated and lanes 4-15 are not.
stance_target: The gap question of whether x8/x16 needs the capacitor mod — it does, and it is PCB rework rather than software
scope_conditions: PCB analysis of the CMP 170HX; mod reproduced by multiple independent modders since April 2026
quoted_support: Twelve of the sixteen PCIe data lanes on the 170HX ship with their AC-coupling capacitors physically omitted from the PCB. There are two capacitors per differential pair, so twelve lanes means 24 missing parts.

claim: The capacitor specification is 220 nF, X7R dielectric, 0402 package, 6.3 V or higher, with Taiyo Yuden MAASJ105SB7224KFCA01 as the confirmed part and Samsung CL05B224KO5NNNC a reported-working substitute; the value is read off the NVIDIA A100 GA100-883 reference schematic P1001-B02 page 3.
stance_target: Whether the mod is a reproducible, specifiable procedure rather than folklore
scope_conditions: Reference designators C1100-C1350 range; PCIe bounds transmitter DC common mode to 3.6 V so 6.3 V carries margin
quoted_support: The value is not guesswork: it is read off the NVIDIA A100 GA100-883 reference schematic P1001-B02 page 3, "IO: PCIe CONNECTOR", which the 170HX board closely follows.

claim: After a complete 24-capacitor mod the link reports LnkSta Speed 2.5GT/s Width x16 while the speed field does not move, confirming the two caps are orthogonal.
stance_target: The claim that a cap-modded but unpatched card is Gen1 x16, not Gen2 x16
scope_conditions: Modded card, no Gen2 unlock installed; verify with lspci -vvv | grep LnkSta
quoted_support: before: LnkSta: Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x4 (downgraded) / after: LnkSta: Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x16

claim: Partial mods negotiate down through the legal widths 16/8/4/1: a card with 12-23 of the 24 capacitors correctly populated trains at x8, and an x8 result indicates incomplete or bridged joints rather than a hardware limit.
stance_target: How to interpret an x8 result after a mod attempt
scope_conditions: One modder's progression across three cards was x4, then x8, then x16 as technique improved
quoted_support: Partial work negotiates down rather than failing. PCIe width negotiation falls back through the legal widths 16, 8, 4, 1, so a card with between 12 and 23 of the 24 capacitors correctly populated trains at x8.

claim: Measured PCIe bandwidth: Gen1 x4 is 0.85 GB/s write / 0.84 GB/s read (clpeak, high confidence); Gen2 x4 is 1.68 GB/s send / 1.71 GB/s receive (OpenCL-Benchmark, medium); Gen1 x16 cap-mod is 2.88 GB/s flat (medium).
stance_target: The repo's ~0.75 GiB/s all-reduce figure, which is consistent with a Gen2 x4 link rather than a Gen1 x4 or x16 one
scope_conditions: clpeak enqueueWriteBuffer/enqueueReadBuffer published 2023 table; OpenCL-Benchmark archived screenshot on an unmodded card
quoted_support: Gen1 x4 | 0.85 GB/s write, 0.84 GB/s read ... Gen2 x4 | 1.68 GB/s send, 1.71 GB/s receive ... Gen1 x16 (cap mod, no Gen2) | 2.88 GB/s flat, error-free

claim: Gen2 x16 has been measured at 6.63-6.67 GB/s (ocl_pcie_bw) with nvtop showing PCIe GEN 2@16x TX 7.061 GiB/s, and a second rig reported 5.97 GB/s on each of four cards — roughly 4x the Gen2 x4 figure.
stance_target: The repo's open question of whether Gen2 x16 would change every communication number ~4x — it would
scope_conditions: Capacitor-modded cards with the Gen2 unlocker installed
quoted_support: Gen2 x16 | 6.63 to 6.67 GB/s (ocl_pcie_bw); the same run's nvtop screenshot shows PCIe GEN 2@16x with TX 7.061 GiB/s. A second rig reported 5.97 GB/s on each of four cards

claim: Gen2 x16 rests on a single observation on 2026-07-26 on one rig in one screenshot, with no lspci capture bridging it to the earlier all-x4 Gen2 survey, no burn-in, no AER counters and no second rig, so its stability is unestablished.
stance_target: Whether a Gen2 x16 result can be relied on for a training run without independent verification
scope_conditions: Single-observation caveat stated by the wiki maintainers
quoted_support: Gen2 x16 has been observed once, on 2026-07-26, on one rig, in one screenshot, on a card whose 24-capacitor mod was complete. There is no lspci capture bridging it to the earlier survey in which every Gen2 result was x4, no burn-in, no AER counters over time, and no second rig.

claim: Tensor and expert parallelism are judged unworkable even at Gen2 x16, so the repo's ruling-out of EP and TP is not an artifact of the x4 link and survives a 4x bandwidth increase.
stance_target: The repo's claim that EP and TP are ruled out by the fabric and that DDP/FSDP are the only training topologies
scope_conditions: Wiki's performance summary; stated as a judgement, not a measurement
quoted_support: Tensor and expert parallelism are judged unworkable even at Gen2 x16.

claim: Pipeline-parallel LLM decode is nearly link-insensitive: a 5120-hidden-dimension model moves 10,240 bytes per token per hop, so saturating a single PCIe 1.0 lane would need roughly 25,000 tokens per second.
stance_target: The repo's implicit assumption that PP is viable on this fabric while TP/EP are not
scope_conditions: Arithmetic from stated model dimensions and PCIe 1.0 lane bandwidth
quoted_support: for pipeline-parallel LLM decode the link is nearly irrelevant (a 5120-hidden-dimension model moves 10,240 bytes per token per hop, so saturating a single PCIe 1.0 lane would need roughly 25,000 tokens per second)

claim: Peer-to-peer is absent on this card and no branch contains any P2P enablement; a PCIe switch fan-out does not create bandwidth because cards behind a switch cannot bypass the uplink without P2P.
stance_target: The repo's claim that the box has no P2P and that all traffic crosses the host bridge
scope_conditions: All observed branches; PEX88096-class switch fan-out considered and rejected
quoted_support: Peer-to-peer is absent on this card and no branch contains any P2P enablement. ... A switch does not create bandwidth, and because the 170HX has no P2P, cards behind one switch cannot bypass the uplink.

claim: No lane fuse is set on the 170HX: OPT_PCIE_LANE_DISABLE (0x00820394), CTRL_OPT_PCIE_LANE (0x0082082C) and STATUS_OPT_PCIE_LANE (0x00820C2C) all read 0x00000000, so the x16 electrical width is intact in silicon and the cap mod is sufficient.
stance_target: Whether the width cap can be defeated in software — it cannot, because no fuse disables the lanes
scope_conditions: Register reads across the card cohort including both 170HX units
quoted_support: No lane fuse is set. OPT_PCIE_LANE_DISABLE at 0x00820394, CTRL_OPT_PCIE_LANE at 0x0082082C and STATUS_OPT_PCIE_LANE at 0x00820C2C all read 0x00000000 on every card in the cohort, both 170HX units included.

claim: No code touches link width: an exhaustive audit of every PCIe-related write in the Gen2 code found LINK_CAP[9:4] Max Link Width never read or written, LNKSTA masked with CLS and DLLLA but never NLW, and a grep for capacitor/AC coupling/solder across master and twelve unreleased branches returns nothing.
stance_target: Any hope of a software-only width unlock
scope_conditions: Audit of shipping master and all twelve unreleased branches
quoted_support: the Max Link Width field at LINK_CAP[9:4] is never read or written, and LNKSTA is masked with PCI_EXP_LNKSTA_CLS and PCI_EXP_LNKSTA_DLLLA but never PCI_EXP_LNKSTA_NLW. A grep of shipping master and all twelve unreleased branches for "capacitor", "AC coupling", "solder" or any lane-width register returns nothing.

claim: A known-good x16 host port still trains the card at x4: measured 2026-07-26, sysfs reported cur 4 / max 16 on both cards and the second GPU's upstream port was itself x16-capable while the link still trained x4.
stance_target: The riser and slot-bifurcation hypotheses for the x4 link
quoted_support: A known-good x16 host port still trains x4. Measured on 2026-07-26 on two cards in one host: sysfs reported the GPU at width cur 4 / max 16 on both, and the second GPU's upstream port was itself x16-capable (cur 4 / max 16) while the link still trained x4.

claim: nvidia-smi reports pcie.link.gen.current/max/width.current as 1,1,4 on a stock card and 2,2,4 with the unlocker; width never moves in either case.
stance_target: The exact pre-flight fingerprint the repo's experiment plans should record
quoted_support: nvidia-smi reports pcie.link.gen.current, pcie.link.gen.max, pcie.link.width.current as 1, 1, 4 on a card with no unlock installed and 2, 2, 4 with the unlocker. Width never moves in either case.

claim: Diagnostic rules: read LnkSta never LnkCap (LnkCap can read Gen2 while the link trains Gen1), do not trust sysfs max_link_speed (reported cur 5.0 GT/s / max 2.5 GT/s on three cards), do not read nvidia-smi 'PCIe Generation Max' as evidence, and the three honest fields are lspci LnkSta, /sys/bus/pci/devices/<bdf>/current_link_speed and nvidia-smi --query-gpu=pcie.link.gen.gpucurrent.
stance_target: The repo's pre-flight instruction to verify negotiated PCIe width/speed per card with lspci -vv
scope_conditions: Wiki diagnostic rules derived from the card cohort
quoted_support: Read LnkSta, never LnkCap. ... Do not trust sysfs max_link_speed. ... Do not read nvidia-smi's PCIe Generation Max as evidence of anything.

claim: Several plausible software causes are ruled out by experiment: NV_PTOP_FS4 0x0002241c does not gate speed, copying A100 board straps made the card undetected at boot, device-ID spoofing fails because FUSE_DEVID_SW_OVR_DIS reads 1, flashing an A100 80GB VBIOS was tested and failed, and a PCIe redriver cannot help because only a retimer could forge TS1/TS2 Rate-ID.
stance_target: The class of software/VBIOS workarounds the repo might otherwise plan around
scope_conditions: Wiki 'Things that look like the cause but are not' section
quoted_support: Copying the A100 strap configuration onto a 170HX resulted in the card not being detected at boot. ... Flashing a genuine A100 80GB VBIOS: Tested and failed. ... A redriver only re-amplifies, so the endpoint still sources its own fuse-capped TX rate.

claim: BAR1 stays at 64 MiB regardless of the framebuffer size the card reports, so full-VRAM host mapping is unavailable even on a card reporting 81920 MiB, and Resizable BAR is advertised but functionally inert.
stance_target: Any plan that assumes host-mapped VRAM or ReBAR on this card
scope_conditions: Config-space survey of stock cards; ReBAR capability present at [bb0 v1] but each BAR advertises one supported size
quoted_support: BAR1 stays at 64 MiB no matter what framebuffer size the card reports, so full-VRAM host mapping is unavailable even on a card reporting 81920 MiB. Resizable BAR is therefore advertised but functionally inert.
